$comment: single source of truth for the desktop release pipeline. the reusable ci workflows and scripts/*.sh all read this file, so adding a platform, a channel, or pointing at a new repo/org is a config edit here — not a workflow rewrite. see docs/RELEASE_GUIDE.md.
$comment_models: ONE bundled model, chosen by measurement rather than by spec sheet. A bake-off on the two flagship jobs -- gap finding under the GBNF grammar, and LaTeX through the plain-text path Scribe actually uses -- ranked this first among Qwen3 0.6B, Gemma 3 1B and Llama 3.2 1B. NEVER bundle a reasoning model (Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1, QwQ): the grammar permits only JSON from the first token, leaving their <think> block nowhere to go, and they return an empty object that parses perfectly. tests/test_model_manager.py guards this. `replaces` is empty because this IS what shipped before; set it when the model changes, or existing installs keep both.
$comment_rolling: The rolling tags are named after their channel, and deliberately match the branch names. Renaming them to beta-latest/nightly-latest split the download path in production: the new build published to beta-latest while the /beta/ landing page, which is generated from MAIN's copy of this file, still wrote /releases/download/beta/ links -- so testers downloaded the previous build. The branch/tag ambiguity these names cause is a developer inconvenience; handing testers the wrong binary is not. Tags no longer trigger any workflow, so the ambiguity costs much less than it did.
